To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
XRCC1 and OOG1 expression was significantly decreased in HNC tumor tissue samples compared to control tissue samples and Ki-67 was overexpressed in HNC tumor tissues compared to control tissues.
the reduced DNA repair capacity (as measured by XRCC1 and OOG1) and enhanced cell proliferation (as measured Ki-67) are associated with the development of HNC in Pakistani population.
XRCC1 and OOG1 are downregulated and Ki-67 is upregulated in head and neck cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between the reduction in DNA repair capacity and enhancement in cell growth, which might be considered as important factor in the development of HNSCC.
exploring the relationship between DNA repair capacity and cell proliferation in HNC cases and controls.
the identification of molecular markers that can be used for the early diagnosis of HNSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduced DNA repair capacity and enhanced cell proliferation are associated with the increased risk of HNSCC development.
downregulation of BER genes and upregulation of Ki-67 expression are associated with increased risk of HNSCC.
the down regulation of BER genes (OGG1 and XRCC1) and the up regulation of proliferation marker Ki- 67 are associated with HNC development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the downregulation of DNA repair genes is associated with the upregulation of proliferation marker Ki-7 in HNSCC.
the downregulation of DNA repair gene XRCC1 and OGC1 is associated with increased expression of proliferation marker Ki-7 in HNSCC patients.
reduced expression of BER genes (as measured by XRCC1 and OOG1) is associated with enhanced proliferation (as measured through Ki-67 expression) and this might play a role in carcinogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reduced DNA repair may play a role in the development of cancer.
XRCC1 and Ogg1 may be used as prognostic markers to predict the outcome of HNC.
XRCC1 and Ogg1 are important factors for head and neck cancer progression.
